page: Microsoft Azure E8pds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the EPDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs powered by a 3.0 GHz Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. The memory configuration includes 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 307 GB SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most multi-core and memory-bound operations. The server achieved average ratings in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark database operations. Memory bandwidth is measured at 566.05 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 91.15 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core performance is a relative weak point, with Geekbench single-core, Passmark CPU, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the bottom 25% tier. LLM inference speeds are also weak, generating 44.28 tokens per second on a small 135M model and 7.51 tokens per second on a 7B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E8pds_v5 offers a high memory-to-vCPU density on an ARM architecture, which typically translates to lower power consumption and resource overhead compared to traditional x86 architectures. Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average database performance, such as 10.98 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, this server is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, caching layers, and static web serving, while being less optimal for single-threaded compute-heavy tasks or machine learning inference.
